findings.title: flight-check re-reads the entire uncapped board once per blocker prefix-miss
findings.evidence: The cap removal (--limit 5000 -> --limit 0) was correct (truncation read as empty), but the replacement query is now unbounded and unfetched per-line: the full-board `br list --json --limit 0` sits INSIDE the per-blocker Consumes loop, so every blocker line whose exact id misses triggers its own full-board read. Measured on this repo's 434-record board: 104KB of JSON, ~66ms per read (br serialize + pipe + first jq parse; streaming jq over the equivalent ledger measured 85ms). So a bead citing K unique-prefix blockers costs (K+1) full-board reads and the consume gate runs on every refined bead in every consuming repo, where boards only grow. The consumer needs two fields (id, status); there is no field projection and no pagination in the call. Same-class site: refly.sh:59 does one full-board read per invocation (bounded, acceptable, noted for the same fix shape).
findings.fix: Hoist one `br_call list --json --limit 0` read before the Consumes loop and resolve every prefix from that cached id list (one jq pass building {id,status}); the per-blocker `br show` for resolved ids stays as-is.

findings.title: assurance-declarations-check re-parses the full 2.6MB ledger per cited PENDING-DECISION id
findings.evidence: The new duplicate-record check makes resolve_pending read the whole ledger TWICE per cited id: a `jq -s` slurp that builds the full array (measured 22ms on this repo's 2.6MB / 434-record board) plus the pre-existing streaming select (85ms), and resolve_pending is called inside two loops (hooks-manifest wiring entries at line 122, orphan hook files at line 157) — O(citations x full board) re-reading a derived file whose record count grows monotonically (closed records included). At ~10-20 citations this adds ~0.5-1.5s to every `lint --changed` pre-commit run, and it re-reads the same file it could parse once.
findings.fix: Slurp the ledger ONCE per run into an id->count map (single `jq -s '{map}' "$BOARD"` exported to a variable), and have resolve_pending consult it for both the duplicate count and existence; keep one final streaming select only for the record body it needs.
